choices.text: You can check back a medium pair and still have a river decision.

questions.explanation: Standard depth still has streets. Short depth often does not.

choices.text: Not putting the stack in with one pair when the board and the action say you are behind.

questions.explanation: Commitment is for hands that are ahead or correctly priced. It is not a mood.

questions.prompt: A 3-bet pot at 100bb has a lower stack-to-pot ratio than a single-raised pot, so…

choices.text: Good one pair commits more often than in a single-raised pot.

questions.explanation: More money is in. The same top pair is stronger relative to the remaining stack.

questions.prompt: Which depth is the usual live open-raise baseline in this academy?

choices.text: About 100 big blinds, with 3–5bb opens when nobody has limped.

questions.explanation: Adjust when the actual stack is far from that baseline. Do not pretend every stack is 100bb.
